title: MovieNet: A Holistic Dataset for Movie Understanding
review_depth: Selective text review: abstract, dataset/task descriptions, §5 p14 and split appendix p47; not all 58 pages read closely.
contribution: Holistic multimodal movie dataset covering 1,100 movies, with character, scene, description and cinematic annotations (abstract).
retention_or_core_mechanism: Dataset and task annotations; not a KV retention method.
evaluation_scope: Movie understanding, scene/entity recognition and movie segment retrieval; paper includes extensive dataset/task appendix.
author_stated_limitations: PDF p14 §5: extend movies and annotations; explore further approaches and movie-understanding topics.
analyst_observed_limits: Inference: movie-level benchmarks alone do not identify whether a streaming failure arose from eviction, perception or narrative reasoning.
candidate_gaps: Evaluation gap: test an independently sourced movie-domain subset with annotated supporting scene intervals before claiming cross-domain retention gains.
already_addressed_by: MovieNet already supplies holistic movie annotations and retrieval tasks; movie evaluation itself is not novel.
cheap_test: CPU: locate 20 accessible movie questions and annotate support scenes; check video access and dataset terms before planning GPU runs.

title: HERMES: KV Cache as Hierarchical Memory for Efficient Streaming Video Understanding
review_depth: Selective detailed review: motivation, layer policy, scoring and §4 setup, conclusion/limitations p9; local code audit is separate evidence.
contribution: Training-free layer-specific sensory, semantic and anchor memory policies motivated by attention analysis.
retention_or_core_mechanism: Shallow recency, middle generic-query semantic importance, deep frame-anchor retention; paper uses 10%/60%/30% layer partition.
evaluation_scope: StreamingBench, OVO and RVS-Ego/movie; offline MVBench, Video-MME and EgoSchema; several LLaVA-OneVision and Qwen2.5-VL sizes (§4).
author_stated_limitations: PDF p9 Limitations: no 72B experiments owing to resources; combinations with orthogonal training-free techniques not investigated.
analyst_observed_limits: Inference: importance similarity and retained-token overlap are diagnostic proxies; downstream accuracy must establish whether changing a scorer helps.
Project implementation gap: current repository scorer behavior must be distinguished from the published policy; see root code audit, not an author claim.
candidate_gaps: Implementation gap: causally propagated generic-query states and correctly aligned positions need downstream QA validation.
Hypothesis, novelty unproven: reuse scorer states until refresh improves quality per unit cost; include auxiliary state bytes and refresh overhead.
Evaluation gap: failures need support-age, evidence-survival and model-capability attribution.
already_addressed_by: The base hierarchical-memory idea, generic query importance and budget-triggered compression are the original HERMES contribution.
InfiniPot already uses injected catalyst prompts for future-unknown importance; newer overlap must be checked in novelty_landscape.md.
cheap_test: Pilot FIFO, current HERMES, corrected scorer and refresh variants on identical 20–30 videos; report paired QA, true peak memory and latency, then decide whether a full run is justified.
duplicate_of_if_identified: HERMES_arxiv.pdf: same title/work, version-level overlap; byte identity not established

title: Ego4D: Around the World in 3,000 Hours of Egocentric Video
review_depth: Selective text review: abstract and dataset/task overview; 91-page supplement not exhaustively reviewed.
contribution: Large-scale egocentric video collection with multiple first-person perception and memory-oriented tasks.
retention_or_core_mechanism: Dataset, annotations and task definitions; no bounded-KV policy.
evaluation_scope: Multiple egocentric benchmarks, including episodic-memory tasks; paper has a large task-specific supplement.
author_stated_limitations: unknown: no sufficiently verified author limitation passage recorded in this bounded pass.
analyst_observed_limits: Inference: common data origin can correlate evaluation outcomes across Ego4D-derived benchmarks; they are not automatically independent domain replications.
candidate_gaps: Evaluation gap: audit source-video overlap across chosen egocentric benchmarks and separate memory retrieval from perception failures.
already_addressed_by: Ego4D already supports episodic-memory evaluation; long-term first-person memory is not a new task.
cheap_test: CPU: deduplicate video identifiers across existing manifests; choose a small non-overlapping evaluation subset.

title: EgoSchema: A Diagnostic Benchmark for Very Long-form Video Language Understanding
review_depth: Selective review: abstract, temporal-certificate motivation/method, evaluation overview and datasheet; primary arXiv identity verified online.
contribution: More than 5,000 human-curated five-option QA pairs on three-minute Ego4D clips; introduces temporal certificate sets.
retention_or_core_mechanism: Temporal certificates characterize the intrinsic video support required by a question rather than equating clip length with difficulty.
evaluation_scope: Long-form multiple-choice video QA; benchmark creation, human/model evaluation and datasheet.
author_stated_limitations: unknown: no explicit author limitation passage reliably isolated.
analyst_observed_limits: Inference: clip length and question timestamp are insufficient proxies for the age or duration of evidence a retention policy must preserve.
candidate_gaps: Evaluation gap: stratify failures by annotated oldest/latest necessary evidence and evidence duration, not elapsed query time alone.
Hypothesis: semantic retention gains should concentrate on questions whose support has aged beyond FIFO capacity.
already_addressed_by: EgoSchema already explicitly argues video length alone does not measure temporal difficulty; support-based temporal evaluation is prior art.
cheap_test: Manually annotate minimal support windows for 20–30 existing failures; compare FIFO/hierarchy outcomes by support age without new training.

title: MVBench: A Comprehensive Multi-modal Video Understanding Benchmark
review_depth: Selective review: abstract, task design and evaluation overview; not an exhaustive appendix review.
contribution: Twenty temporally challenging video tasks, using task definitions and conversion of public annotations.
retention_or_core_mechanism: Evaluation tasks designed to require temporal reasoning beyond single-frame understanding.
evaluation_scope: Multi-task video understanding and VideoChat2 evaluation.
author_stated_limitations: unknown: no explicit author limitation passage verified.
analyst_observed_limits: Inference: temporal-task accuracy is a useful control but does not itself isolate bounded streaming eviction.
candidate_gaps: Evaluation gap: ensure a proposed memory improvement preserves short-term action/order ability as well as long-term retrieval.
already_addressed_by: Temporal reasoning tests and single-frame insufficiency are already core MVBench design goals.
cheap_test: Run a small task-stratified subset with matched sampled frames and token budgets; include frame-order perturbations only where labels remain interpretable.

title: VILA: On Pre-training for Visual Language Models
review_depth: Selective review: abstract, principal pretraining findings and evaluation overview.
contribution: Studies interleaved pretraining, language-model updating and text instruction blending for visual language models.
retention_or_core_mechanism: Pretraining and instruction tuning rather than inference-time retention.
evaluation_scope: Image VLM generalization, in-context learning and related multimodal evaluations.
author_stated_limitations: unknown: no explicit limitation passage verified.
analyst_observed_limits: Inference: backbone training affects perception and in-context reasoning; a weak backbone can hide gains from memory retention.
candidate_gaps: Evaluation gap: identify questions wrong even with uncompressed/recent support available before attributing errors to eviction.
already_addressed_by: Better pretraining/interleaved data and retaining text ability are prior work; not a feasible original training project within a few rented GPU days.
cheap_test: Compare full/relevant-window input against bounded input on the same small failure sample using an available backbone.

title: MiniCPM: Unveiling the Potential of Small Language Models with Scalable Training Strategies
review_depth: Selective review: abstract, training/scaling overview and explicit limitations p18.
contribution: Studies 1.2B/2.4B non-embedding-parameter language models and scalable training including warmup-stable-decay learning rates.
retention_or_core_mechanism: Training scaling and scheduling; not a video-memory mechanism.
evaluation_scope: Small language model evaluation and scaling studies.
author_stated_limitations: PDF p18 Limitations: scaling study was not extended by training an LLM to validate the law; WSD application to LLMs not fully explored.
analyst_observed_limits: Inference: language-only scaling findings do not establish video KV retention behavior for a particular multimodal 0.5B backbone.
candidate_gaps: Evaluation gap: separate small-backbone reasoning limits from retention-policy limits using available larger-model pilot controls.
already_addressed_by: Small-model training efficiency is established work; reproducing scaling training is not the intended low-budget original contribution.
cheap_test: Use an existing stronger checkpoint for a tiny oracle-support comparison; do not train a new language model.

title: How Far Are We to GPT-4V? Closing the Gap to Commercial Multimodal Models with Open-Source Suites
review_depth: Selective review: abstract, architecture/training overview and evaluation scope.
contribution: Open-source multimodal suite improves visual-language performance through architecture, data and training recipes.
retention_or_core_mechanism: Model training and multimodal representation rather than a fixed-memory streaming policy.
author_stated_limitations: unknown: no explicit limitation passage verified.
analyst_observed_limits: Inference: stronger spatial perception and resolution can change apparent memory-policy headroom.
candidate_gaps: Evaluation gap: use oracle evidence and matched-resolution controls before treating every wrong answer as lost memory.
already_addressed_by: Open multimodal model scaling and data curation are already central to InternVL1.5.
cheap_test: Tag OCR, fine spatial detail and answer reasoning errors in the existing both-wrong set; test a few with cropped/oracle evidence.

title: Video-MME: The First-Ever Comprehensive Evaluation Benchmark of Multi-modal LLMs in Video Analysis
review_depth: Selective review: abstract, benchmark construction, modality/duration table and discussion pp1–3; local version v3 is dated 30 May 2025 although first arXiv submission is 2024.
contribution: 900 videos and 2,700 manually annotated MCQs across six domains; evaluates short, medium and long videos with subtitle/audio settings.
retention_or_core_mechanism: Benchmark modality and duration stratification, not memory management.
evaluation_scope: Videos from 11 seconds to one hour; three questions per video; short/medium/long groups of 300 videos (PDF pp2–3).
author_stated_limitations: PDF p3 discussion reports performance declining with increasing video length and proposes better long-context architectures and temporal-reasoning training; this is an empirical observation/future direction, not a formal limitations section.
analyst_observed_limits: Inference: duration trends conflate evidence density, sampling, modality availability and eviction unless these are controlled.
candidate_gaps: Evaluation gap: report visual-only and subtitle/audio-enabled settings separately and align frame sampling when comparing memory policies.
already_addressed_by: Duration and modality-stratified evaluation are already part of Video-MME; adding a long-video benchmark alone is not original.
cheap_test: Select a small duration-stratified visual-only subset, retain identical sampling and record support age; add subtitle controls only if supported by the actual pipeline.

title: VideoLLaMA 2: Advancing Spatial-Temporal Modeling and Audio Understanding in Video-LLMs
review_depth: Selective review: abstract, connector/audio method overview, evaluation descriptions and caption-evaluation passage; 29 pages not exhaustively reviewed.
contribution: Spatial-temporal convolution connector and audio understanding branch address temporal and multimodal video understanding.
retention_or_core_mechanism: Trained connector and audio-video modeling; not training-free visual KV eviction.
evaluation_scope: Video QA/captioning and audio-related evaluations; long appendix.
author_stated_limitations: unknown: no explicit author limitations passage verified.
analyst_observed_limits: Inference: audio-dependent failures cannot be repaired by retaining more visual KV entries alone.
candidate_gaps: Evaluation gap: classify missing modality versus evicted evidence before prioritizing memory interventions.
already_addressed_by: Audio integration and spatial-temporal connectors already exist; adding audio is not an unoccupied novelty claim.
cheap_test: On 20 both-wrong items, label whether answer requires audio/subtitles, tiny visual detail, temporal relation or distant visual support.

title: VideoLLM-online: Online Video Large Language Model for Streaming Video
review_depth: Selective review: online setup, method/evaluation overview, domain discussion p8 and explicit Appendix D limitations p19.
contribution: Online video-language formulation processes an ongoing stream and supports timely responses instead of only end-of-video questions.
retention_or_core_mechanism: Streaming dialogue training and response scheduling; learned method rather than a drop-in KV policy.
evaluation_scope: Streaming video dialogue, including activity-oriented first-person settings.
author_stated_limitations: PDF p19 Appendix D: inadequate high-quality streaming dialogue data limits generalization; generated dialogues miss varied real-world requirements; small-data overfitting; spatial ability weak with fewer spatial tokens.
analyst_observed_limits: Inference: replayed timestamped QA does not establish asynchronous real-time interaction, silent periods or deadline behavior.
candidate_gaps: Evaluation gap: measure update throughput and query response latency under a simple arrival schedule, in addition to offline QA.
Evaluation gap: spatial detail versus temporal capacity needs matched-token controls.
already_addressed_by: Online video dialogue and response scheduling are already established here; they cannot alone be claimed as a new contribution.
cheap_test: Replay 2–3 existing videos with fixed wall-clock frame arrival and injected questions; log backlog, missed deadlines and peak memory.

title: LLaVA-OneVision: Easy Visual Task Transfer
review_depth: Selective review: abstract, model/task-transfer setup and video evaluation overview; 43-page supplement not exhaustive.
contribution: Consolidated single-image, multi-image and video model with transfer between visual task settings.
retention_or_core_mechanism: Shared trained visual-language model; not a streaming retention policy.
evaluation_scope: Broad visual tasks across image/multi-image/video; extensive supplementary results.
author_stated_limitations: unknown: no explicit author limitation passage verified.
analyst_observed_limits: Inference: general video transfer does not guarantee stable attention-scoring semantics under repeated eviction and cache compaction.
candidate_gaps: Implementation/evaluation gap: validate scorer changes on the actual backbone and positions used rather than extrapolating a mechanistic observation across families.
already_addressed_by: Cross-task visual transfer and this backbone are prior work; HERMES already evaluates LLaVA-OneVision variants.
cheap_test: Log a small prefix with actual backbone attention and compare selector decisions plus paired QA; count all auxiliary memory.

title: Video-CCAM: Enhancing Video-Language Understanding with Causal Cross-Attention Masks for Short and Long Videos
review_depth: Selective review: abstract, projector/masking method, length-generalization description and conclusion p10.
contribution: Causal cross-attention masking in a trained video projector improves temporal consistency and length generalization.
retention_or_core_mechanism: Causally masked cross-attention projector, distinct from HERMES generic-query scorer masks.
evaluation_scope: 4B/9B/14B models; training with 16 frames and evaluation extending to 96 frames.
author_stated_limitations: unknown: no explicit author limitation passage verified; PDF p10 conclusion summarizes causal temporal projector.
analyst_observed_limits: Inference: causality must be specified at the exact layer and operation; a causal projector result is not proof that a custom KV scorer is correct.
candidate_gaps: Implementation gap: test the repository scorer with allowed causal history and proper positions; evaluate QA rather than assuming a mask is sufficient.
already_addressed_by: Causal cross-attention for temporal consistency already exists here; causality in itself is not new.
cheap_test: Unit-level attention inspection on one short prefix plus downstream small QA pilot with causal versus current scorer under equal budget.

title: Kangaroo: A Powerful Video-Language Model Supporting Long-context Video Input
review_depth: Selective review: abstract, curriculum/data overview and evaluation framing.
contribution: Data curation and curriculum improve a video-language model supporting longer video input.
retention_or_core_mechanism: Training curriculum increases input frames/resolution; not a bounded unknown-future-query KV policy.
evaluation_scope: Long-context video-language evaluation for an 8B-scale model.
author_stated_limitations: unknown: no explicit author limitation passage verified.
analyst_observed_limits: Inference: more input capacity or better temporal training does not establish a fair fixed-memory retention comparison.
candidate_gaps: Evaluation gap: equalize actual visual evidence, frame sampling and total memory when comparing a bounded policy with a long-context model.
already_addressed_by: Long-video curricula and increased frame support are prior approaches, requiring training outside the immediate low-budget plan.
cheap_test: Use available model checkpoints only as a small oracle/context control; report differing compute and do not call unmatched models retention-policy baselines.

title: VideoLLaMB: Long Streaming Video Understanding with Recurrent Memory Bridges
review_depth: Selective review: abstract, memory/SceneTiling method, §3.6 p6, conclusion p8 and training appendix p13; primary arXiv identity/version verified online (v2 revised 2025).
contribution: Memory bridge layers and temporal memory tokens encode streaming video; SceneTiling segments semantic units.
retention_or_core_mechanism: Learned recurrent memory bridge plus semantic segmentation; distinguish trained bridge from training-free use of SceneTiling.
evaluation_scope: VideoQA, egocentric planning and Needle in a Video Haystack (NIAVH); synthetic one-second needles across depth/length at 1 fps (PDF p6 §3.6).
author_stated_limitations: PDF p8 conclusion: further integration of LLM memory with memory bridges is a future direction, not a formal limitation claim.
analyst_observed_limits: Inference: a synthetic one-second needle can test retention but does not by itself cover natural distributed evidence, causal relations or low-FPS missed events.
Feasibility observation: Appendix C p13 describes training using four A800 GPUs; full retraining is outside the stated short single-GPU budget.
candidate_gaps: Evaluation gap: extend existing needle controls with natural support windows, multiple jointly necessary events and fixed memory accounting.
Hypothesis: semantic scene transitions predict when a cached importance state becomes stale; must compare against fixed refresh and random schedules.
already_addressed_by: Controlled depth/length video needle tests already exist in NIAVH; recurrent memory and semantic scene segmentation are established.
cheap_test: CPU annotate support first; small inference-only experiment moving the same visible evidence to different ages while guaranteeing it survives sampling.

title: InfiniPot: Infinite Context Processing on Memory-Constrained LLMs
review_depth: Selective detailed review: abstract, §3 mechanism, evaluation setup/prompt ablation and §6 limitations; primary arXiv identity verified online.
contribution: Continual Context Distillation retains context within fixed memory without further training.
retention_or_core_mechanism: Catalyst Prompt (CaP) injected before cache limit estimates future importance; Novelty under Compression (NuC) emphasizes novel information (PDF p2).
evaluation_scope: Text LongBench and needle-in-haystack; context length used as KV-memory proxy; prompt variants include general and question-aware prompts (§4).
author_stated_limitations: PDF p9 §6: predefined compression ratio may be suboptimal; very long-term dependencies not exhaustively tested; actual on-device deployment not evaluated.
analyst_observed_limits: Inference: prompt-guided unknown-future relevance predates HERMES; text evidence does not establish video-stream scorer freshness or compute gains.
Inference: actual bytes/latency may differ from token-count proxies when a method carries extra query states or compressed representations.
candidate_gaps: Paper-stated gap: investigate adaptive compression, but novelty is now crowded and must be checked against recent work.
Hypothesis, novelty unproven: adaptive refresh of a propagated generic-query state may improve net QA per latency under video changes.
Evaluation gap: include auxiliary state, peak allocated/reserved memory and refresh work, not KV entries alone.
already_addressed_by: CaP already uses temporary generic prompts for future-unknown KV importance; novelty also enters selection via NuC.
Adaptive compression is an explicitly proposed direction, not evidence it remains unsolved in 2026.
cheap_test: Compare current prompt scoring, causal propagated scoring, fixed-interval reuse and adaptive reuse on identical videos; include refresh-only cost and a random schedule with matched refresh count.

title: StreamingBench: Assessing the Gap for MLLMs to Achieve Streaming Video Understanding
review_depth: Selective review: abstract, taxonomy/construction pp1–5 and evaluation framing; primary arXiv identity verified online; appendix not exhaustively reviewed.
contribution: 18 tasks, 900 videos and 4,500 human-curated questions; five questions at different timestamps per video.
retention_or_core_mechanism: Taxonomy of real-time visual, omni-source and contextual understanding; timestamped queries rather than a retention algorithm.
evaluation_scope: 13 proprietary/open models in original paper; real-time, audio/video and conversational-context tasks.
author_stated_limitations: unknown: passages criticizing previous VStream-QA are not author-stated limitations of StreamingBench and must not be mislabeled.
analyst_observed_limits: Inference: aggregate timestamped MCQ accuracy does not identify the location/age of necessary support or guarantee a live system keeps pace with input.
Project evidence boundary: local 498-video/2,495-question run is a subset and configuration, not the full 900-video benchmark.
candidate_gaps: Evaluation gap: separate visual-only task coverage from omni-source/contextual coverage and state exclusions explicitly.
Evaluation gap: annotate support windows and dialogue dependency for failed questions; prevent future-frame and future-question leakage.
Evaluation gap: pair QA scores with processing throughput, response latency and true state memory.
already_addressed_by: Streaming task taxonomy, audio/contextual questions and timestamped queries already exist; a new benchmark claim requires a distinct validated measurement.
cheap_test: Audit dataset/task manifests and 20–30 failures; verify each question sees only its prefix and allowed dialogue, then bootstrap paired differences at video level.
